paradigms.inShort: Before you change a habit, look at the lens you already see through. The book calls that lens a paradigm. These exercises show how it shapes what you do and what you get.

h1.inShort: Habit 1 is about choosing how you respond, instead of letting things decide for you. You'll notice where you can make a difference, and act there on purpose.

h2.inShort: Habit 2 is about knowing where you're headed before you set off. You'll write down what you stand for and the roles that matter to you. Then your daily choices point somewhere.

h3.inShort: Habit 3 turns what matters most into a weekly plan. You'll make time for the important things, not just the loudest ones.

h4.inShort: Habit 4 looks for deals where both sides come out ahead. You'll practise agreements where nobody has to lose.

h5.inShort: Habit 5 is about really listening before you make your own case. You'll practise hearing someone out fully, then asking to be heard.

h6.inShort: Habit 6 is about combining different views into something better than either one. You'll practise treating differences as a source of new ideas.

h7.inShort: Habit 7 is about looking after yourself: body, mind, heart and spirit. You'll build small routines that keep you going, instead of running on empty.

interdependence.inShort: Working well with others takes trust, and trust grows in small steps. You'll track the small things that build it or wear it down. The book calls this an Emotional Bank Account.
